headline: Skyroot rockets to Unicorn status with $60 million fundraise; Trilegal, TT&A, CAM advise
sum: Skyroot Aerospace, India's leading private space launch provider, raised $60 million co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and GIC, achieving $1.1 billion valuation and unicorn status. The capital will scale manufacturing, establish high-cadence Vikram-1 launches, and develop the Vikram-2 cryogenic launch vehicle.
implication: Cross-border tech-infrastructure deal structure with strategic institutional (GIC, BlackRock) and domestic (Greenko, Shanghvi) co-investors; precedent for Indian aerospace company reaching unicorn via institutional APAC/global venture rounds; regulatory oversight under DOS/IN-SPACe framework expected but not disclosed in article.
detail: Skyroot Aerospace, a Hyderabad-based private aerospace manufacturer offering on-demand satellite launch services via its Vikram series rockets, raised $60 million from a consortium led by Singapore-based Sherpalo Ventures and GIC (Government Investment Corporation of Singapore), alongside BlackRock-managed funds, founders of renewable-energy unicorn Greenko Group, Arkam Ventures, Playbook Partners, and the Shanghvi Family Office. The fundraise values the company at $1.1 billion, conferring unicorn status. The capital is earmarked for high-cadence Vikram-1 launch operations, manufacturing scale-up, and development of Vikram-2, a 1-tonne-class vehicle with advanced cryogenic propulsion. The deal was driven by three tier-1 Indian law firms, each advising different stakeholders.

framework.ref: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) — Licensing & Regulation
framework.note: Central. Private sector space launch operations require IN-SPACe authorization and compliance with Department of Space guidelines; commercial launch provider status triggers regulatory gating.

framework.ref: FEMA 1999, Schedule 5 (Liberalized Remittance Scheme) & Schedule 4 (Overseas Investment)
framework.note: Central. Inbound FDI from GIC (Singapore sovereign fund), BlackRock (US), and global investors requires FEMA compliance; outbound repatriation and profit routing subject to RBI/FEMA approval.
Central. Issuance of equity to new investors requires board approval, shareholder authorization (if threshold met), and compliance with pricing rules for preferential allotment.
Relevant if any investor funds relate to non-resident Indian (NRI) donors or foreign entities with restrictions on India-specific activity; aerospace/defence nexus warrants review.

framework.ref: Bharatiya Reserve Bank (Foreign Exchange Management) Rules 1999 — Schedule 1 (LRS) & Overseas Remittance
framework.note: Central. Profit repatriation, dividend distribution, and upstream capital transfers from the company to foreign investors subject to FEMA Schedule 1 route (Liberalized Remittance Scheme for individuals) or Schedule 4 (corporate).

framework.ref: Department of Space (DoS) — Commercial Space Activities Approval
framework.note: Central. Skyroot must hold valid IN-SPACe authorization to conduct satellite launch services; fundraise value and foreign investor participation may require DoS/ISRO notification.
Tangential. While primarily for aviation, launch vehicle testing and certain aerospace operations may intersect with DGCA oversight; space launch vehicles typically under DoS purview.

framework.ref: Technology Transfer & Export Control (Satellites & Launch Vehicles)
framework.note: Amended. Indian aerospace/launch vehicles subject to ECRA (Export Control Regulation) and potential DSIR/DoS authorization; foreign participation in R&D or IP transfer requires approval.

structure.consideration: $60 million equity investment; post-money valuation $1.1 billion (unicorn threshold).
conditions: IN-SPACe authorization and Department of Space compliance (if commercial launch operations ongoing).
FEMA Schedule 4/5 approval for inbound foreign investment (GIC, BlackRock funds, global investors).
Shareholder approval for preferential allotment of shares (if triggered under Companies Act 2013, Section 62).
Board authorization for share issuance and investor rights (governance, liquidation preference, board representation).
Technology transfer / IP ownership verification (given aerospace/space-launch nexus).
Clearance from relevant security/defence authorities (if applicable to sensitive aerospace activities).
approvals: IN-SPACe (Department of Space) — for ongoing commercial launch authorization and any foreign investor involvement in sensitive space technology.
FEMA (RBI) — for inbound FDI from GIC, BlackRock, and other foreign funds; profit repatriation route.
Board of Directors & Shareholders (if required) — for preferential allotment under Companies Act 2013.
Regulatory clarity on foreign investment limits in aerospace (if any sectoral cap applies).
structure.novel: Indian private-sector space company achieving unicorn valuation via Singapore sovereign wealth fund (GIC) and global institutional co-leadership; first major $60M+ round for Indian commercial launch provider; strategic domestic co-investor participation (Greenko, Arkam) alongside international VCs signals infrastructure-tech hybrid positioning.

triggers.note: Private launch provider status requires explicit regulatory authorization; foreign investor participation in space-launch equity may trigger additional DoS review.
Inbound FDI from Singapore, US, and global funds must comply with Schedule 4 (corporate FDI route); upstream repatriation subject to RBI approval.
Equity issuance to new investors requires board approval and, if applicable, shareholder consent for preferential allotment pricing.

triggers.law: Export Control Regulation Act (ECRA) & Technology Transfer
triggers.note: Aerospace/launch vehicle technology may fall under controlled goods; foreign investor participation and IP ownership subject to DSIR/DoS oversight.
